_metadata.description: P1 requirements — records absorption, run linkage, operator surfaces, and the multi-space embedding refinement. All planned; validation entries declare intended evidence without asserting refs that do not exist. Note: id P1-009 is intentionally vacant. Harness memory import was promoted to P0 as VMEM-P0-011 (D-022); the id was retired rather than reused, and P1-010 was not renumbered, so that existing cross-references stay valid and no reader mistakes a renumber for a different requirement.

requirements.title: Work-record memory kind
requirements.description: A work-record memory kind carries the fields the swarm-manager records contract defined — trigger, approach, evidence, outcome — validated as a required set at write. This replaces `swarm-manager records create` as the agent-facing verb so agents learn one write surface. Backlog association is derived from run correlation rather than a hand-passed flag, which is the failure this absorption is designed to fix.

validation.notes: A work-record note missing a required field is rejected with a field-specific error.
A work-record written inside a run resolves its backlog association from correlation with no flag passed.
Migration review: existing swarm-manager records import as work-record memories with narrative and outcome preserved.

requirements.title: Run correlation and sibling events
requirements.description: A memory written inside an agent run stores the receipt correlation emitted automatically by api-core — run id, workflow execution id, actor kind. Retrieval exposes a command that lists the other events from that run. Memory stores identifiers only and never a denormalized copy of run data, so there is exactly one truth about any run.

validation.notes: A write carrying run correlation persists the ids and no copied run payload.
A write with absent correlation (operator shell, null run id) succeeds and stores no correlation.
The sibling-events command resolves a stored run id to the other events of that run.

requirements.title: Tree descent
requirements.description: Zooming a summary renders that node's immediate constituents — leaves verbatim, child summaries as summaries labeled with their span and depth — and descent repeats to the leaves. A reader must never mistake a summary for an original, so every rendered summary is labeled as one.

validation.notes: Zoom on a depth-2 node returns its immediate children, not its transitive leaves.
Rendered summary nodes carry an explicit summary label with span and depth; leaves do not.

requirements.title: Supersession-aware summarization
requirements.description: When a candidate cluster contains contradicting entries, the summarization prompt resolves by recency rather than conjoining both claims. Because clustering is semantic, near-identical contradictions co-occur in the same cluster, so resolution is always a within-cluster judgment and never a corpus-wide contradiction search.

validation.notes: A cluster containing a claim and its later negation summarizes to the later claim only.
A cluster of compatible claims summarizes without dropping the distinct claims it can fit in budget.
Operator review of summarization output on a real cluster sample, distinguishing intended fact dropping from fact mutation.

requirements.title: Multi-space facet embedding
requirements.description: Several short derived texts per memory — topic, rule/implication, entities — are each embedded normally rather than conditioning one vector on an instruction. This yields multiple neighbourhoods per memory using the embedding model already deployed fleet-wide, and keeps the derived texts human-readable so bad clustering is debuggable. Embeddings intended for clustering use the model's clustering task prefix rather than the document prefix.

validation.notes: A memory produces one embedding per derived facet text, each retrievable and attributable to its source text.
Clustering-purpose embeddings request the clustering task prefix; retrieval-purpose embeddings request the document prefix.
Two memories related only on one facet co-cluster in that facet's space and not in the others.
Clustering groups two memories that agree on the entities space while disagreeing on topic, which is the purpose clause: more than one notion of relatedness.
Spaces are paired by index and the shorter side bounds the comparison, so a summary's single space never scores against a leaf's entities framing.
Recall takes the best space, so a query matching a secondary framing outranks a partial primary match.

requirements.title: Operator review surface
requirements.description: A UI for browsing the journal as a timeline, inspecting the frontier so the compaction staircase is legible, and correcting a memory's facet or pinned state. Correction is the operator's control over what the fleet believes; a misclassified standing rule is the highest-consequence error the system can make, so re-facet and pin/unpin are first-class actions rather than admin afterthoughts.

validation.notes: Journal timeline renders loading, empty, partial, and error states.
Frontier explorer distinguishes leaves from summaries and shows each summary's span and depth.
Re-facet and pin/unpin actions round-trip to the API and reflect in the rendered state.

requirements.title: Harness prompt-block install
requirements.description: A command installs and updates the prompt block in each harness convention file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and equivalents). The block describes WHAT is worth remembering and MUST NOT instruct the agent to call a specific memory command. Telling an agent to use a foreign write verb is an instruction-compliance problem — it may comply, may not, or may write to both stores and fork memory silently. Describing what to remember lets the agent use its native memory tool, which it does reliably, and the harness domain captures that write. The block is idempotent and delimited so re-running updates in place rather than appending duplicates.

validation.notes: Installing twice leaves exactly one delimited block with the current content.
Installing into a file with unrelated content preserves that content outside the delimiters.
The rendered block contains no imperative to invoke a memory CLI command, guarding the describe-what-not-how contract against drift.

requirements.title: Harness write capture
requirements.description: Native memory writes made by an agent through its own harness tooling are captured into the journal. Two channels, selected per harness by the capability matrix in docs/concepts/INTEGRATIONS.md: a pre-write hook where the runtime exposes one, and store diff as the universal floor. Hook install rides the existing per-resource permissions machinery under resources/<agent>/cli/internal/permissions/, which already ships pretooluse-bash-deny.sh for claude-code and grok — this scenario extends that layer and never touches agent binaries. Capture is required, not hardening: single-blob harnesses (Codex, opencode) cannot be diffed reliably into discrete memories, so for those runtimes a hook is the only precise channel.

validation.notes: A native memory write in a hook-capable harness appears in the journal without the agent invoking any memory command.
With the hook disabled, the same write is still captured by the next store-diff sweep — degraded latency, no loss.
Per-runtime verification of which harnesses expose a usable pre-write surface; findings update the capability matrix.

requirements.title: Pinned-set bounding by curation
requirements.description: The pinned set is bounded by operator curation rather than by compaction, because a rule the system is obliged to display unconditionally cannot be safely auto-merged or auto-evicted. Three mechanisms, each terminating in an operator decision: (1) consolidation proposals — the cohesion scoring the forest already computes is run over pinned entries and surfaces near-duplicate groups as merge proposals, never as automatic collapses; (2) renewal — each pin carries a review date and lapses to unpinned rather than deleted when not reconfirmed, so a lapsed rule stays a searchable standing-rule memory and the mechanism fails safe; (3) a pin budget that returns a trade-off against the weakest current pins when a new pin would exceed it. The budget is the forcing function: without it the first two are optional and therefore skipped, which is the failure mode measured on `--backlog-ref` in D-001. The binding constraint is attention, not tokens — a wake view with fifteen standing rules is read and one with three hundred is skimmed — so this limit binds well below the overflow reported by `VMEM-P0-006`.

validation.notes: Near-duplicate pinned entries surface as a merge proposal and are never collapsed without operator confirmation.
A pin whose review date passes without reconfirmation becomes unpinned, remains in the journal, and remains retrievable by recall.
Reconfirming a pin extends its review date without creating a duplicate journal entry.
A pin request that would exceed the budget returns the weakest current pins as a trade-off proposal rather than silently pinning or silently refusing.
Lapse and merge both change wake output while leaving every affected journal entry intact and searchable.
Calibrate the budget and review interval against a real pinned set; both initial values are unvalidated.
